target.title: fix(web-search): align credential presence with usable providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine opencode` reported no accepted/actionable findings after the optional-chain cleanup.

## Proof

- Added regression coverage for Google/Gemini-vs-Vertex manifest env scoping: `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` alone is false for selected `gemini`, while `GEMINI_API_KEY` is true.
- Provider-scoped manifest env detection now first reads the selected bundled web-search provider's public contract env vars, then falls back only to same-provider manifest setup/auth env metadata when a public contract is unavailable.
- Existing policy/credential tests still cover plugin allow/deny, disabled entries, keyless providers, raw plugin webSearch credentials, SecretRefs, and explicit provider selection.



### Follow-up Evidence - 2026-07-11

- Commit `cbd771ef20` rejects explicitly configured unknown web-search providers before top-level or nested credentials can satisfy the credential-presence audit.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 30 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted but blocked by the local invalid OpenAI API key (401); OpenCode autoreview on the same local patch returned clean with no accepted/actionable findings.



### Follow-up Evidence - 2026-07-11 nested auto provider

- Commit `50ad8c1064` rejects unknown nested auto-mode provider credentials before they can satisfy the credential-presence audit.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 30 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(sessions): derive list channels from agent keys
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking `sessions_list` to show archived or gateway-less group/channel sessions could see the channel reported as `unknown` when the only available routing metadata was an agent-scoped session key such as `agent:main:slack:channel:...`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sessions list channel fallback now derives from the request-key portion of canonical agent session keys before reading the existing `<channel>:(group|channel):...` shape. This keeps explicit `channel`, delivery context, and `lastChannel` precedence unchanged, and matches the Gateway sibling behavior for the same session-key contract.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the changed helper, `sessions_list` caller path, Gateway sibling parsing, and focused regression test.

## User Impact

`sessions_list` results now keep useful channel labels for agent-scoped Slack, Discord, Telegram, and similar group/channel sessions even when older or lightweight rows do not carry separate channel metadata.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `sessions_list` derives `channel: "slack"` from an agent-scoped group/channel session key when the Gateway row lacks separate `channel`, `origin.provider`, `deliveryContext.channel`, and `lastChannel` metadata.
- Current head: `af8e15a0922baf31b1bbce02a748e2bf937070c2`.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts`
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main`
  - Repo-local runtime transcript through the real `sessions_list` tool with a redacted Gateway `sessions.list` row:

```json
{
  "head": "af8e15a0922baf31b1bbce02a748e2bf937070c2",
  "tool": "sessions_list",
  "gatewayMethods": [
    "sessions.list"
  ],
  "requester": "agent:main:main",
  "input": {
    "key": "agent:main:slack:channel:C123:thread:1710000000.000100",
    "kind": "group",
    "spawnedBy": "agent:main:main",
    "separateMetadataPresent": {
      "channel": false,
      "originProvider": false,
      "deliveryContextChannel": false,
      "lastChannel": false
    }
  },
  "output": {
    "count": 1,
    "key": "agent:main:slack:channel:C123:thread:1710000000.000100",
    "kind": "group",
    "channel": "slack",
    "spawnedBy": "agent:main:main",
    "sessionId": "sess-redacted"
  }
}
```

- Observed result: focused Vitest passed with 1 file / 9 tests; diff hygiene passed; autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings; the runtime transcript shows the real `sessions_list` tool returning `channel: "slack"` from the agent-scoped key.

target.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where invalid SMS webhook posts could consume the same inbound callback quota used by signed Twilio callbacks when deployments receive traffic through a shared proxy address.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SMS webhook now parses and validates Twilio-signed form requests, confirms the configured account, and only then applies the fixed-window quota. The quota key is scoped to the SMS account and webhook route plus the client address so one account path cannot consume another account path's quota.

## User Impact

Operators using the SMS plugin keep the same Twilio signature validation and webhook responses, while invalid unsigned traffic no longer burns the quota for later valid callbacks. High-volume valid signed callbacks are still rate-limited per account route.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --idle-timeout 90m --ttl 240m --timing-json --shell -- "corepack pnpm test extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts"`
- AWS Crabbox `run_c56fe73f9596`, lease `cbx_979b5ad08666`, `c7a.8xlarge`: `extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts` passed 4 tests.
